Quick update from infra after initial triage:
- Root cause signal: dedicated-reserved-us-west-3 pool saturation due to an unexpected workload spike and a suboptimal batching profile from the customer's long-running jobs. Kernel selection is hitting a slower execution path under the observed sequence length distribution.
- Current headroom: ~12% available but fragmented across nodes; immediate single-pool scaling will take ~50–70 minutes to fully provision and warm caches.

Mitigations we can enact now (ordered by speed):
1) Failover routing: divert 25% of PulseCommerce traffic to hosted-us-west-1 model variant (10–15m to start). Pros: quick availability. Cons: weaker SLAs / different quantization profile may cause subtle regressions.
2) Emergency oversubscribe/burst on reserved pool: add 1 additional node group and prioritize PulseCommerce tokens (ETA 45–75m to be fully effective). Requires approval for temporary overcommit and billing override.
3) Model fallback: serve a slightly older model artifact (lower mem footprint) for non-critical routes — 30–40m to rollout with smoke tests.

Recommendation: start (1) immediate routing of 25% traffic to hosted variant and (2) begin provisioning oversubscribe while we monitor error rate. If both fail to reduce errors below 5% in 60m, we escalate to full-burst and consider account-level credits.

Attachments: pool-metrics-20261114.csv (snapshot), infra-ops-checklist.pdf (operation playbook)
